title: Ribbon runs: First qualifying slip
summary: String runs. Find the first number at least k.
descriptionMd:
Inputs
`line` is text. A character is one letter, digit, space, or punctuation mark.

Your tasks
1. Create a list `runLengths`. A run is a group of matching characters next to each other. End a run only when the character changes or the text ends. Record the length of each run, from left to right. Spaces count as characters too. For "aa bb", `runLengths` is [2, 1, 2].
2. Read `runLengths` from left to right. Find the first number that is at least `k` and store that number, not its position, in `firstMatch`.
3. Complete `ribbonRunsFirstQualifyingSlip` so it returns `firstMatch`. Return it, do not print it.

Example
If `line` is "zu  gid" and `k` is 1, then `runLengths` is [1, 1, 2, 1, 1, 1] and `ribbonRunsFirstQualifyingSlip` returns 1.

Rules
- If no number is at least `k`, return -1.
- `k` (a whole number from 1 to 8) is the threshold in task 2: compare each number with it.

Test data
TEST DATA 1: `line` is "niizx xvvvi" and `k` is 4.
TEST DATA 2: `line` is "II iII" and `k` is 1.

constraints: k is a whole number from 1 to 8. Answers fit in a signed 32-bit integer: -2,147,483,648 through 2,147,483,647.
The text uses ASCII characters (a basic character set). Only an ordinary space separates words.
Efficiency goal: time O(n); extra memory, including the helper list, O(n). n is the input length. These labels describe how work and memory grow with the input.
